title: Singapore's Progress on COP28 Pledges on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuel, Increasing Renewable Energy Capacity and Improving Energy Efficiency
what_it_is: Singapore's Progress on COP28 Pledges on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuel, Increasing Renewable Energy Capacity and Improving Energy Efficiency

sections.label: COP28 goals and Singapore plans
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment about Singapore's progress on renewable energy and energy efficiency and plans to meet COP28 goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in view of the call by the UN Climate Change Conference 2023 (COP28) to accelerate zero and low emission technologies (a) what has been the progress in Singapore to increase renewable energy capacity and to improve the overall rate of energy efficiency; and (b) what are the plans ahead to accelerate towards the COP28 goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what are the plans for operationalising the UAE Consensus from COP28 including the transition away from fossil fuels to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050; and (b) what is the timetable for this transition in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment how will Singapore contribute to global efforts agreed at the global stockttake at the 2023 UN Climate Change Conference (COP28) to (i) transition away from fossil fuels to achieve net zero by 2050 in keeping with the science (ii) triple renewable energy capacity globally and double energy efficiency by 2030 and (iii) phase down unabated coal power, reduce methane emissions and phase out inefficient fossil fuel subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The UAE Consensus calls on countries to transition away from fossil fuels, accelerate the phasedown of unabated coal power, phase out inefficient fossil fuel subsidies and to triple renewable energy and double energy efficiency globally by 2030, among others.

sections.label: Singapore carbon tax increase
sections.summary: The carbon tax was raised to $25 per tonne from 1 January 2024 and will rise to between $50 and $80 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: I am glad that Members, including those from the Opposition, who advocated for a carbon tax above $100 per tonne, agree that more should be done to support our net-zero goals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We have raised our carbon tax to $25 per tonne from 1 January 2024 and will progressively raise it further, to between $50 and $80 by 2030.

sections.label: Singapore solar power deployment
sections.summary: Singapore has doubled solar power deployment since 2021 to over 1,000 megawatt-peak currently under the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Singapore has been accelerating our energy transition as part of the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We have doubled our solar power deployment since 2021 to over 1,000 megawatt-peak (MWp) currently.

sections.label: Conditional approvals for electricity imports
sections.summary: Last year the Government issued Conditional Approvals for 4.2 gigawatts of imports from Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Last year, the Government issued Conditional Approvals for 4.2 gigawatts of imports from Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam.

sections.label: Fossil fuel transition language
sections.summary: Transitioning away from fossil fuels is a major achievement, and the global stocktake brought a louder call to accelerate action this decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Transitioning away from fossil fuels is one major achievement – it is the first time that such language has appeared.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: But more importantly, it is that with a global stocktake, there was a louder and more concerted call to accelerate action in this decade.

sections.label: Global renewable and efficiency goals
sections.summary: Goals such as tripling renewable energy capacity and doubling energy efficiency improvements are global collective measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Where we have goals, such as three times renewable energy capacity, two times energy efficiency improvements, these are global collective measures.

sections.label: Nuclear energy decision and capabilities
sections.summary: No decision has been made on adopting nuclear energy, but Singapore is building capabilities to understand how these technologies advance and could help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: These are two very important metrics that feed into our energy decision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We have not made a decision on adopting nuclear energy, but we are building capabilities to understand how these technologies are advancing and also, how these technologies can potentially be of help to Singapore.

sections.label: FAST-P climate finance initiative
sections.summary: Senior Minister Teo announced an initiative called FAST-P to galvanise up to $5 billion in seed funding and blended finance for climate action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Senior Minister Teo has announced an initiative called "FAST-P" to basically galvanise up to $5 billion in seed funding and also in blended finance to help in climate action.

sections.label: Supporting AOSIS on loss and damage
sections.summary: Singapore will not contribute grants in loss and damage but will support developing countries, particularly the Alliance of Small Island States, to tap the fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: That is where Singapore's strength and role as a financial centre can come into play.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, we do not think that our current capacity or resources would be meaningful in contributing grants in L&D, but we definitely will be supporting other developing countries, particularly in the Alliance of Small Island States (AOSIS) grouping, to tap on the L&D fund because they are most badly affected.

sections.label: Biennial transparency report and NDC
sections.summary: The question asks about the Government's shorter-term goals before Singapore's first biennial transparency report in 2024 and its updated NDC at COP30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: My second supplementary question is that moving forward, what are the Government's shorter-term goal and emphasis in the run-up to the submission of Singapore's first biennial transparency report in 2024 later this year and also as we submit our updated NDC at COP30?

sections.label: Hydrogen as alternative fuel
sections.summary: In the power generation system, provision is being made for hydrogen to be introduced as an alternative fuel.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: But there are certain areas that we want to invest in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, as I have mentioned in my speech, already in our power generation system, we are making provision for hydrogen to be introduced as an alternative fuel.

sections.label: MAS taxonomy for transition energy
sections.summary: MAS and banks are working on a taxonomy to finance transition energy and fuels, but neighbouring countries decide their own pace and investment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Our Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) as well as our banks are working actively to look at how we can have a taxonomy that allows transition energy and transition fuels to be financed so that, as the Member said, neighbouring countries that still have a lot of coal-fired power plants are able to benefit from finance to help them transit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: There are many, many opportunities for us to play a role.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: But ultimately, the decision, pace, direction and investment decisions have to be taken by the respective countries.

sections.label: MSE monitoring ITMs alignment
sections.summary: The question asks whether MSE monitors ITMs for alignment with net-zero by 2025 goals and COP28 consensus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could I ask whether MSE is monitoring these ITMs to make sure they are aligned with our goals of reaching net-zero emissions by 2025, and also whether they are now consistent with the COP28 consensus that the Minister just talked about?
